title: French Beef Stew with Red Wine, Carrots and Mushrooms
summary: A rustic French-style beef stew with a deep red-wine sauce, sweet carrots and earthy mushrooms. It’s rich, savoury and ideal for a slow, comforting dinner.
steps: Pat the beef dry and season it with half the salt and the black pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef well in batches, then transfer it to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium and add the onion. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until softened and lightly golden. Add the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute more.
Pour in the red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Simmer for 3 minutes.

Add the beef back to the pot along with the carrots, bay leaves, thyme and water. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover partially and cook for 90 minutes, stirring now and then, until the beef is starting to soften.
Add the mushrooms and the remaining salt. Cook uncovered for 20 to 30 minutes more, until the beef is tender and the sauce has reduced.
Mix the cornstarch with the water to make a smooth slurry, then stir it into the stew and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce lightly thickens.
Remove the bay leaves and serve hot with crusty bread or mashed potatoes, if desired.
